text: Every big financial decision starts in a spreadsheet.
And somewhere in it, there is a cell nobody checked.
One formula divided by the wrong number. $6.2 billion lost.
say: One formula divided by the wrong number. Six point two billion dollars, lost.

text: One missing minus sign. A capital loss reported as a capital gain.
None of them was fraud. They were spreadsheet errors.
We built it for the people who build financial models, review them, and make decisions on what they say.
But it works for anyone whose numbers have to be right. If you work in Excel, it works for you.
Thousands of formulas. Dozens of tabs. And no time to trace every one by hand.
You could ask a chatbot. It will sound convincing.
But language models are built to reason, not to calculate.
A financial model doesn't need a plausible answer. It needs a proven one.
Meet Model X-Ray.
The debugger for financial models.
Here is a real one. A power purchase agreement model, with 2,400 formulas and three errors we planted.
say: Here is a real one. A power purchase agreement model, with two thousand four hundred formulas, and three errors we planted.

text: No question needed. It reads every sheet and labels every line.
It finds the suspects and works out the cause.
Then it proves each fix: it changes a copy, recalculates the whole workbook, and tries to break its own answer.
Three planted errors. Three found.
The cell. The cause. The fix. And the evidence behind it.
Not sure? Ask it.
You decide: approve, edit or reject. Approved fixes go to a corrected copy. Your original file never changes.
Inside, two minds work together.
NVIDIA Nemotron does the thinking. A calculation engine does the maths.
say: NVIDIA [Nemotron](/nˈimoʊtɹɑn/) does the thinking. A calculation engine does the maths.

text: Nemotron maps the model, judges every suspect and tells a real error from a deliberate choice. Then a second Nemotron, the Verifier, tries to break every fix before you see it.
